improvement_notes: Qualify the opening claim that forward kinematics calculates the end-effector position “exactly” by stating that this is exact only for the assumed geometric model and coordinate convention; the later caveat is accurate but should appear earlier.
Introduce the base/world coordinate frame explicitly before presenting the equations, including the positive counterclockwise convention and the assumption that the base is fixed.

The generated schematic’s instruction to “trace the signal or idea from left to right” may imply a block diagram or data-flow diagram, while the lesson primarily teaches geometric composition. Replace that instruction with geometry-specific guidance.

Add a brief numerical check or instructor answer for the target-reaching challenge. Students can experiment, but a target near (0.30, 0.30) benefits from a stated tolerance and one verified example solution.
Clarify that the plotted workspace bounds are only visualization limits, not a complete workspace calculation; joint limits and self-collision are not represented by the program.
Mention the required installation or environment for matplotlib and provide a text-only fallback, such as printing the calculated coordinates, to improve beginner accessibility.
The lesson is strong but somewhat repetitive around relative angles, radians, and model limitations. Consolidating one or two repeated explanations would improve pacing without reducing rigor.

For deeper progression, briefly distinguish a planar pose from a full spatial 3D pose and note that the displayed orientation is the tool-frame orientation only under the assumed rigid, aligned gripper model.
